Patent ductus arteriosus The ductus arteriosus is a vascular channel present in the fetal circulation that connects the pulmonary artery and the descending aorta. In some infants the ductus arteriosus fails to close, a condition known as persistent patent ductus arteriosus. Details of its management are given on p.68. Peripheral arterial thromboembolism Occlusion of the peripheral arteries may occur due to em- bolism or thrombosis (see Thromboembolic Disorders, p.1187). Sudden or acute occlusion causes reduction of blood flow to the distal portions of the limb and may lead to critical limb ischaemia. Emergency treatment with sur- gery or thrombolytic drugs is often required to restore blood flow and preserve the limb.
